clusters.name: Teodor's death, 1978–1979
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather Teodor's death in January 1978, within the following year: your grandmother Delphine stopped cooking and went to your mother's every evening; your father took night shifts and distanced from your mother; your uncle Anton's drinking worsened with a warning at work; your uncle Anton and aunt Celeste separated in August; your mother's anxiety rose over your mother and Anton; and your brother Callum's ear infections began. These shifts spread across the family in the months after the death, each one's trouble near another's.

clusters.name: Odette's bed rest, 1984–1984
clusters.reason: Around your mother's bed rest in March 1984, within the following months: your grandmother Hazel came every morning to keep the house; your father argued with his mother over how she kept it; and your brother Callum stammered again after a year free of it. These shifts pile up in spring and early summer 1984 around your mother's loss of functioning.

clusters.name: Hazel's Parkinson's diagnosis, 1986–1996
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Hazel's diagnosis in September 1986, over the following decade: your grandfather Ambrose took over her cooking and appointments; your father phoned his father every night for news; your father and uncle Lyle argued over who should help their parents; your grandfather Ambrose developed chest pains; your father drank most evenings; your grandfather gave up his workshop and hardly left her side; and your father fought with your mother over his evenings at his parents' house. The trouble builds slowly, with shifts spreading from your father's worry to his drinking and his conflict with your mother as your grandmother's illness deepened.

clusters.name: Callum's move north, 1999–2000
clusters.reason: Around your brother Callum's move in May 1999 for a job at the mines: your father and brother argued most nights over the plans; your mother could not settle at the thought of him so far away; your father missed days at work and sat up late in the garage; your sister Ines skipped school most of that autumn; your mother took Ines with her everywhere; and your sister Ines returned to school full days and passed her exams by August 2000. The trouble moves from your brother's leaving through your parents' conflict and anxiety to your sister's falling away and then recovery.

clusters.name: Hazel's death, 2003–2003
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Hazel's death in January 2003, within the following months: you could not sleep more than a few hours; you stopped going to the bookshop and were let go in May; you dreaded buses and crowded shops and went out only after dark; and you took a job at the garden centre and slept through the night again by November. Every shift in these months is yours, and no one else's shows then.
